I found an issue here, when you turn off, while the device is off it will turn it on. I will check this issue and ad a validation if needed

Edit: I fix the issue and push the changes.

The general idea is ok, there are two issue though:

1. You currently cannot trust power state. It reports the wrong value sometimes, e.g. when you have a HomePod connected as a speaker. It is also not implemented for DMAP (it just returns Unknown), so it won't work with Apple TV 3 or earlier at all.
2. From an API point of view, you need to check the features interface if `turn_on` and `turn_off` are supports. Just assuming they are will break with Apple TV 3 and earlier as they are not implemented there. It's described [here](https://pyatv.dev/development/features/).

Power management is generally quite iffy and I would suggest to add it as an option, but allow people to opt-out (or in) if it doesn't work.

Thanks @postlund for the comment
> You currently cannot trust power state. It reports the wrong value sometimes, e.g. when you have a HomePod connected as a speaker. It is also not implemented for DMAP (it just returns Unknown), so it won't work with Apple TV 3 or earlier at all.

For that case I fallback to the previous solution, so we don't "lose" anything. I though of making a solution with coordinator that also pool the state, but I prefer to start with the simple solution.

> From an API point of view, you need to check the features interface if turn_on and turn_off are supports. Just assuming they are will break with Apple TV 3 and earlier as they are not implemented there. It's described here.

I did it first, but then I thought of removing the feature check, and in case the feature is not implemented it will bubble an error to the user, IMO, it is better than ignoring and not giving feedback, WDYT?
I can add a comment about that if agreed.

> Power management is generally quite iffy and I would suggest to add it as an option, but allow people to opt-out (or in) if it doesn't work.

If it doesn't work you "opt-out" since - 
For state update - it will be the same as before
For state changes (turn on / off) - it will bubble error to the user instead of disconnect / connect HA from device (IMO, I don't think that this is expected behaviour)

> For that case I fallback to the previous solution, so we don't "lose" anything. I though of making a solution with coordinator that also pool the state, but I prefer to start with the simple solution.

Assuming you consider the value of power state at all, that unfortunately does not hold. The case with the HomePod means that power state will continue to be turned on, even when turning the device off (I.e when you do that from the device, via the physical remote for instance or using `turn_off` in pyatv).

I'm not sure I totally understand what you mean with coordinator and "pool the state", can you elaborate a bit on that?

> I did it first, but then I thought of removing the feature check, and in case the feature is not implemented it will bubble an error to the user, IMO, it is better than ignoring and not giving feedback, WDYT?
> I can add a comment about that if agreed.

To me, that sounds like poor experience as that will *always* generate an error in the log when turning an Apple TV 3 on or off, even though we can check if those features are supported or not and call if they are.

> If it doesn't work you "opt-out" since -
> For state update - it will be the same as before
> For state changes (turn on / off) - it will bubble error to the user instead of disconnect / connect HA from device (IMO, I don't think that this is expected behaviour)

Same as I mentioned earlier, we should not give an error for something that isn't an error. State updates will have the mentioned problem as we cannot trust it. An option allows the user to either opt-in to experimental support that might work for some people, but easily get out of it in case it doesn't work as expected. In the latter case, we can at least tell them exactly what they get (which might not match what they desire) which is far better user experience than "maybe" getting something that works and potentially errors or unexpected behavior they can't get out of. I'm not saying that what is currently on master is good, but it's predictable across the line.

@postlund thanks for your feedback. 

> Assuming you consider the value of power state at all, that unfortunately does not hold. The case with the HomePod means that power state will continue to be turned on, even when turning the device off (I.e when you do that from the device, via the physical remote for instance or using turn_off in pyatv).

So you saying that HomePod issue (and other devices) means that the state will be stuck on "turn on" and not "unknown"? If we are sure about that, we can use the below solution (coordinator and pooling)
Another thing about this point: In case of HomePod issue, if the state is always stuck on turned on and not off, the turn off operation will still work (since it will pass the condition), but it will also turn on, in case it was off already (a bug that we can live with?)

> I'm not sure I totally understand what you mean with coordinator and "pool the state", can you elaborate a bit on that?

**Edit**: after searching more about the issue, my solution probably wouldn't work... so you can skip that - 

Using [CoordinatorEntity](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data/#coordinated-single-api-poll-for-data-for-all-entities) to scheduling a pooling and actively fetch the state of the device (not sure how to do that yet), afaik, it should work for HomePod issue, but need to check that.
If it works, we can turn the coordinator by default, and if we can push update about power management we can turn off the coordinator.

> To me, that sounds like poor experience as that will always generate an error in the log when turning an Apple TV 3 on or off, even though we can check if those features are supported or not and call if they are.

Yeah, I agree, I can return in supported_features function a value with or without TURN_ON | TURN_OFF feature based on avt's supported command (I'm not sure how its effecting UX).
Another solution (that I don't like) is in case that it's not supported use a flag that indicate what is last operation that happened, on or off.
IMO it will be better to keep the system automatic without user intervention for opt out/in, since I can know if the user can turn on or not (as mentioned by atv's api)

WDYT?

Hi @postlund ,
I made some changes according our conversation:
1. Turn on and off will call only if the feature is available
2. If a power management updates received at least once, media player will start to "respect that", so it will turn off only if the tv is on already. If we never got power management updates, we can assume that this is the HomeKit case, and the behaviour will change accordingly.

review_comments: Any reason why you check this here and not in `turn_on` (or vice versa)?

Yes, in turn on - if it will be executed when it's already on, nothing will happen
But, in turn off, if turn off will be executed and the state is already off it will turn it on (while we want to keep the tv off)
